evidence: Structure verified against frozen bytes (.qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r5/task/tests) by parsing every TOML with tomllib in memory. scoring.toml:1-11 has [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0, [weights] functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2 (sum 1.0), [floors] functional=0.05; every name has its directory (tests/gates/render, gates/constraints, scored/functional, scored/polish, scored/visual). All five judge.toml: [judge] judge="claude-code" fallback (matches REWARDKIT_JUDGE in task.toml:31), mode, timeout, isolated=false, prompt_template="prompt.md" which exists and contains {criteria} and {app_context}; no model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight in [judge]; no extra top-level tables or criterion keys. Each declares the playwright stdio MCP server (playwright-mcp --headless --isolated --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium --no-sandbox), identical to the template; tests/Dockerfile (byte-identical to template) installs @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and links /usr/local/bin/chromium. Only scored/functional/judge.toml:14-18 declares the verifier server: command /usr/local/bin/python3, args ["/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py", "$APP_RESTART_HELPER"]; test.sh:191-193 chmods the generated helper, removes its .used marker and exports APP_RESTART_HELPER before run_suite (test.sh:203-227); RewardKit 0.1.7 expands it with os.path.expandvars at mcp add (local copy deliverables/colderwater-playground-devtools/final-cross-check-2026-09-27/harness/rewardkit-0.1.7-source/agents.py:66; tests/Dockerfile:31 pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7). test.sh, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/Dockerfile and .dockerignore are byte-identical to the frozen template. Criteria: gates have 1 binary criterion each (hro_gate_render, hro_gate_shared) with aggregation all_pass; functional 15 binary criteria, unique ids, weights 2-5.5 (all positive, sum 61), weighted_mean; polish 5 binary, weights 1.5-2, weighted_mean; visual 5 likert points=5 weight 1, weighted_mean; no empty descriptions. Only hro_intake_restart (functional judge.toml:31) instructs restart_app; functional prompt.md:1 limits restart_app to the criterion that says so; marker-based single use survives per-session MCP respawns. Deviation from template: functional uses mode="individual", timeout=600 (template: batched, 9000). RewardKit 0.1.7 models.py:142 JudgeMode accepts "individual"; judges.py _arun_agent_individual runs one claude -p call per criterion sequentially with the per-call timeout, MCP registration persists (ClaudeCodeCLI.cleanup is a no-op), and functional/prompt.md:9-11 was rewritten for one-criterion sessions. Serial worst case 15x600=9000 = the canonical functional budget; 9000+900+900=10800<11100 scored wrapper; 600+600<1500 gates; 1500+11100=12600<13200 verifier (task.toml:27). Lessons file applied: prompt sizes (lesson 10) measured with app_context substituted: largest batched assembly 36,186 B (functional if batched), largest single functional session 14,198 B, all far under 128 KB; checker-not-fixer paragraph (lesson 6) present at line 7 of all five prompts; gates are single simple criteria (lesson 4); weights are not a single 1.0/1.5/2.0 scheme (lesson 2) but that is a weighting-policy row matter, not structure. Workbook: frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx Quality Checks row 25 (#24) text read; Internal Quality Checks row 25 carries the retired reward.toml wording (pinned judge, valid aggregate) - interpreted for the staged layout; the skill asset copy differs in bytes but has the same row 24 text. Risk remains: no full configured RewardKit run on these bytes exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope says full configured grading/workload is absent), so the individual-mode wiring, the 600 s per-criterion cap for long criteria such as hro_intake_restart (gate + many steps + restart in one session), the restart MCP invocation in the real verifier, and three-retry schema-mismatch overruns are NOT EXERCISED. Owner should confirm the mode/timeout change from the template is recorded as authorized and that check-batched-independence-wording accepts the one-criterion-per-session wording.
